FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 20 January 1989, after the draft finalized by the Glass Containers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council. This standard lays down the requirements for glass jars for packing This standard has been revised to bring it in line with the current this revision, vacuum lug finish has been prescribed in addition vacuum lug type of finishes are being used increasingly because of sealing giving longer shelf life to the product. Also, it provides the jams, jellies and marmalades. manufacturing practices. In to RONPP neck finish. The obvious advantages of vacuum ease of opening and closing.

REQUIREMENTS

IS 7511 ( Part

6.1 Pattern
The jars shall be of the pattern as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. The design of the jar shall be such that the lumps of the material can be easily taken out with a spoon. 6.2

IS 7511 ( Part

IS 10133

Methods of test for the determination of brimful capacity of glass containers by gravimetric method Methods of thermal shock tests for glass containers

The glass jars shall be symmetrical around the axis with uniform distribution of glass all over the walls and the base shall rest on a plane surface without rocking. 6.3 The sealing surface shall be smooth and suitably radiussed at both the outer and the inner peripheries of glass with a minimum of 0'8 mm Rat surface. It shall also be free from prominent seam marks. 6.4 The tolerance limits on the planity deviation for the sealing surface shall not exceed 0'4 mm. The planity of the top sealing surface of the glass jars shall be checked by the method given in Annex A. 6.5 The tolerance to 10133 : 1982. 1 on height shall be according

IS 11930 : 1986

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standards, the definitions given in IS 6654 : 1972 shall apply. 4 MATERIAL The glass jars shall be transparent and shall be free from greenish tint as far as possible. They shall also be free from cracks and shall be

FINISH

The jars shall have roll on non-pilferproof type neck finish of size 58 as laid down in IS 7511 ( Part 3 ) : 1986. Alternatively, the glass jars shall be provided vacuum lug finish of nominal diameter 53 or 63 mm conforming to IS 7511 ( Part 8 ) : 1986. 8 TESTS 8.1 Limit of Alkalinity

METHOD A-l APPARATUS OF CHECKING PLAINITY DEVIATION OF SEALING SURFA%E

A-l.1 The following apparatus is needed for checking the plainity deviation of sealing surface of the glass jar: a) Standard surface plate plane glass plate, and b) Feeler gauge 0'64 mm. A-2 PROCEDURE A-2.1 Invert the empty glass jar placing the sealing surface on top of the surface plate or glass plate. or 6 mm thick from 0'05 to

A-2.2 Lightly press the base of the container on the side opposite to one at which the measurement is being taken. A-2.3 Insert the feeler gauge (starting from 0'05 mm ) between the glass sealing surface and the surface plate until the thickest possible feeler gauge just slides in.
NOTE-The feeler gauge shall not be forced in.

set ranging

A-2.4 Record the maximum clearance obtained between the glass sealing surface and the surface plate by rotating the jar through 360" while keeping the base of the jar lightly pressed on the side opposite to one at which the measurement is being made.

Standard

Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
